instruction: The PG bootstrap seed path writes the school grade as a Persian WORD ("دهم", "یازدهم") into INTEGER grade columns on classes and subjects, so an empty PG + bootstrap path fails with a type error and boot stops. Map the twelve Persian grade names to their ordinal numbers deterministically; unknown values stay fail-closed.

In the multi-instance OTP ratelimit harness, each instance builds its own JWT key and uses it as the OTP pepper when PAYESH_OTP_PEPPER is unset. Code that instance A hashes fails verification on instance B, so the cross-instance shared-code test R8c only stayed green because of the 0000 bypass. Add an explicit shared PAYESH_OTP_PEPPER to the harness config so it simulates real deployment behavior.
output:
```
fix(A-02): shared OTP pepper in otp-ratelimit harness + docs regen

R8c claimed to test a code issued by instance A being accepted on
instance B, but each boot() builds its own JWT key, and the OTP pepper
falls back to that key when PAYESH_OTP_PEPPER is unset. Different peppers
=> the hash A wrote is not verifiable on B. Before the A-02 fix this was
invisible because the default-on 0000 bypass made any login succeed.
With the bypass opt-in only, the false green is gone; an explicit shared
pepper now models a real deployment. Result: 47 pass / 2 fail
(R10a/R10b pre-existing legacy-hash cases).

Also regenerates DATA_DICTIONARY.md (schema drift: processing_at,
processing_token) and DOCS_HEALTH_REPORT.md, and refreshes the single
affected row of the rc44 freeze manifest (LF-normalised hash).
```

+    PAYESH_DEMO_CODE: '1',

+       سبز می‌شد. pepperِ صریحِ مشترک، رفتارِ واقعیِ استقرار را شبیه‌سازی
